channel.title: SecurityWizardry Vulnerability Radar (RMFconsultoria)
channel.description: Alertas de vulnerabilidade (CVSS) - fonte NVD (fallback quando o SecurityWizardry está bloqueado) - RMFconsultoria

item.title: CVE-2026-123579 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | DNSSEC validation in Hickory DNS hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 and hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 does not distinguish NODATA responses from wildcard-expanded positive responses. For a query that should return NODATA in a zone with wildcard records, an attacker can combine an NSEC3 record matching the query name with a signed wildcard record into a bogus positive response that validation accepts.

item.title: CVE-2026-123580 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | Hickory DNS hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 and hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 perform insufficient checks on NSEC3 record names during DNSSEC verification, comparing only the hashed label without confirming the record belongs to the correct zone. Attackers can supply NSEC3 records from another zone with a matching hash label to forge DNSSEC nonexistence proofs.

item.title: CVE-2026-123581 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 contain a DNSSEC validation flaw that accepts a response as a positive answer when any valid RRset appears in the answer section, without checking that the RRset is responsive to the query. Attackers can supply signed but unrelated RRsets so that responses lacking matching records are validated as positive answers instead of as no-data responses.

item.title: CVE-2026-123582 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | The validating recursive resolver and validating forwarder in Hickory DNS (hickory-server) 0.25.0 before 0.26.2 do not check whether the SOA record passed DNSSEC validation when assembling NXDOMAIN or NODATA responses. An attacker able to supply forged DNS responses can have a forged SOA record returned to clients with the AD bit set, misleading clients that rely on the server's DNSSEC validation.

item.title: CVE-2026-123583 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | The recursive resolver in Hickory DNS hickory-recursor 0.25.0 through 0.25.2 and hickory-resolver 0.26.0 before 0.26.2 does not apply out-of-bailiwick filtering to negative responses. Attackers able to supply crafted negative responses can include out-of-bailiwick records to facilitate cache poisoning and more easily exploit other DNSSEC verification flaws.

item.title: CVE-2026-123584 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2 | The hickory-net crate in Hickory DNS 0.26.0 before 0.26.2 stops listening and returns an error when a client UDP connection receives a datagram that cannot be parsed as a DNS message. Remote attackers who guess the query's source port, without knowing the transaction ID, can spoof malformed responses to abort client queries, causing denial of service.

item.title: CVE-2026-123585 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | The hickory-resolver component of Hickory DNS 0.25.0 before 0.26.2 follows irrelevant CNAME records when resolving recursive queries, sending queries that are unnecessary to answer the original request. Attackers controlling DNS responses can include CNAME records in the authority or additional sections, or outside the original query name's CNAME chain, causing excess resolver queries and increased query amplification.

item.title: CVE-2026-123586 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | Hickory DNS 0.25.0-alpha.3 through 0.25.2 contains a query amplification vulnerability in its recursive resolver, which mishandles cyclic sibling name server referrals that lack glue records. Attackers controlling two zones whose name servers reference each other without glue records can make the recursor loop, sending many upstream queries, amplified further by zero-TTL NS records.

item.title: CVE-2026-123587 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.9
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.9 | The DNSSEC validation in the Hickory DNS hickory-net crate 0.26.0 before 0.26.2 identifies wraparound NSEC records by comparing the next domain name to an SOA record in the response, accepting that SOA even if it fails validation. Attackers who can supply DNS responses can combine a genuine NSEC record and its RRSIG with a crafted SOA record to forge nonexistence of any RRset.

item.title: CVE-2026-123588 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | The recursive resolver in Hickory DNS (all versions of the hickory-recursor crate, and hickory-resolver 0.26.0 before 0.26.2) caches an empty connection pool when it follows a referral with no glue records and all queries for the name servers' IP addresses fail. An attacker able to spoof DNS responses can make these lookups fail, causing all subsequent queries for the affected zone to fail until the cache entry expires or is evicted.

item.title: CVE-2026-123589 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | The DNS-over-QUIC (DoQ) server in hickory-server (hickory-dns) before 0.26.2 does not apply any timeout when reading a request message from a QUIC stream, bypassing all configured timeouts. A remote unauthenticated client can open a connection and a request stream and hold it open indefinitely, consuming server resources and causing a denial of service.

item.title: CVE-2026-123590 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Hickory DNS hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 and hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 accept NSEC and NSEC3 records for DNSSEC nonexistence proofs when any other record with the same owner name passes signature validation. Attackers able to supply DNS responses can mix validly signed records with bogus same-name NSEC or NSEC3 records of different types in the authority section to forge nonexistence proofs.

item.title: CVE-2026-123591 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2 | Hickory DNS hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 and hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 fail to verify, per RFC 6840 §4.4, that an NSEC or NSEC3 record denying a DS RRset also proves the delegation's NS record exists. Attackers can reuse child-side NSEC or NSEC3 records to fake an insecure delegation and forge child-zone records.

item.title: CVE-2026-123592 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2 | The hickory-net crate in Hickory DNS 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 allows DNSSEC validation bypass because Name's Hash ignores label lengths and ValidationCacheKey compares only that hash. An attacker controlling an unsigned delegation whose name differs from a signed target only in dot positions can prime an Insecure verdict, causing forged answers for the target to skip signature verification instead of returning SERVFAIL.

item.title: CVE-2026-123593 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Hickory DNS hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 and hickory-proto 0.24.0 through 0.26.0-alpha.1 compare DNSKEY public keys against DNSSEC trust anchors without checking the DNSKEY record name, so an RRset made up only of trusted keys is accepted without RRSIG verification. Attackers able to spoof or control name server responses can replace a secure zone's DNSKEY RRset with the root zone's keys, and use a large TTL to keep it cached.

item.title: CVE-2026-123594 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 contain an NSEC validation flaw that returns a secure proof for NXDOMAIN responses when the covering NSEC's Next Domain Name is a strict descendant of the query name, which actually proves the name exists as an empty non-terminal. On-path attackers can flip the unsigned rcode of a genuine signed NODATA response from NOERROR to NXDOMAIN, causing validators to accept forged nonexistence of the name.

item.title: CVE-2026-123595 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.25 through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 contain a DNSSEC validation flaw in the validating recursor's NSEC3 handler, which matches the closest encloser by hash alone without checking the type bitmap and so accepts parent-side ancestor-delegation NSEC3 records as proof of nonexistence. An attacker who delivers one response built from genuinely signed parent NSEC3 records can cause NXDOMAIN or NODATA to be cached with AD=1, denying resolution of existing names at and below the zone cut.

item.title: CVE-2026-123596 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 contain a DNSSEC validation flaw in the validating recursor's NSEC handler that accepts parent-side ancestor-delegation NSEC records as proof of nonexistence for names below the zone cut. An on-path attacker, rogue parent nameserver, or attacker winning a port and TXID race can deliver one forged NXDOMAIN response built from genuinely signed parent NSEC records, causing authenticated denial of existing child-zone names cached for the negative TTL.

item.title: CVE-2026-123597 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.25.0-alpha.1 through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net before 0.26.2 contain a logic bug in DnssecDnsHandle's DS-fetch path that caches transient DS lookup errors as Bogus DNSSEC validation verdicts. An attacker who induces a SERVFAIL, REFUSED, or timeout response to a child-zone DS sub-query causes the validator to return SERVFAIL for all names under that zone until the cache entry's TTL expires.

item.title: CVE-2026-123598 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | The validating recursor in Hickory DNS hickory-recursor 0.25.0 through 0.26.0-alpha.1, hickory-resolver 0.26.0-alpha.1 before 0.26.2, and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 caches DNSSEC-bogus answers using the untrusted, attacker-supplied record TTL (capped at 24 hours) instead of a short validation-failure TTL. A remote attacker who spoofs a single authoritative response with an invalid signature and a long TTL can keep the bogus result cached for up to 24 hours.

item.title: CVE-2026-123599 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto before 0.26.0-beta.1 and hickory-net before 0.26.2 contain a DNSSEC validation bypass because verify_rrsets() ignores DNS class when partitioning RRsets, so non-IN records skip signature verification yet are marked secure when the IN records verify. Attackers able to supply DNS responses can include forged CH or HS class records, including DS records, to authenticate any DNSKEY and forge child zone responses.

item.title: CVE-2026-123600 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.25.0-alpha.3 through 0.25.2 and hickory-net 0.26.0-alpha.1 before 0.26.2 contain a DNSSEC validation flaw in DnssecDnsHandle that accepts NSEC3-signed NODATA responses for zone-apex queries as secure without an NSEC3 record matching the hashed QNAME. On-path attackers or malicious authoritative servers can replay a validly signed non-apex NSEC3 with the zone's signed SOA to serve an authenticated (AD=1) denial of any apex RRtype for the negative-cache TTL.

item.title: CVE-2026-123601 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.3 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.25.0 through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 invert the relational operators in the wrap-around branch of find_covering_record() in nsec3.rs, so the last NSEC3 record in a zone's hash ring covers every hash except its owner. Attackers able to inject DNS responses can replay that NSEC3 record and its RRSIG to forge DNSSEC-validated negative responses denying legitimate names.

item.title: CVE-2026-123602 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2 | The Hickory DNS recursor in all versions of hickory-recursor and in hickory-resolver 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 (recursor feature) is vulnerable to ghost domain names attacks because it reuses child-side apex NS RRsets cached from zone NS queries for iterative resolution. By repeatedly querying a zone's NS records, an attacker keeps the stale RRset cached indefinitely, letting name servers whose delegation the parent revoked keep answering for the zone.

item.title: CVE-2026-123603 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | hickory-proto and hickory-resolver 0.26.0 before 0.26.2, hickory-server 0.25.0-alpha.1 before 0.26.2, and hickory-recursor 0.25.0-alpha.3 through 0.26.0-alpha.1 fail to canonicalize IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses when checking deny_answers, deny_server, or AccessControlSet rules. Attackers can use IPv4-mapped addresses to evade answer filtering, trigger queries to denied nameservers, or reach hickory-server library deployments on dual-stack IPv6 sockets from denied clients.

item.title: CVE-2026-123604 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | Hickory DNS hickory-resolver 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 contains an unbounded retry loop in NameServerPool::try_send, which re-queues truncated (TC) responses without checking the answering transport or counting iterations. A malicious authoritative server returning TC=1 on every transport keeps the resolver spinning on a persistent TCP connection until the 5-second request deadline expires, causing resource exhaustion.

item.title: CVE-2026-123605 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.1 through 0.25.0-alpha.3 and hickory-net before 0.26.2 contain a DNSSEC validation bypass because the validator verifies an RRSIG against the DNSKEY of whatever name appears in its Signer's Name field without checking that this name is the zone containing the RRset. Attackers controlling any secure zone can produce valid signatures over arbitrary records in unrelated zones, which resolvers, recursors, and clients using DnssecDnsHandle accept as authenticated.

item.title: CVE-2026-123606 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | The hickory-dns recursor in hickory-recursor 0.25.0-alpha.3 through 0.25.2 and hickory-resolver 0.26.0-alpha.1 before 0.26.2 iterates every out-of-bailiwick NS target lacking glue in a referral without any per-query work budget. Remote attackers can serve such referrals to force A and AAAA lookups per target, amplifying traffic against remote servers or exhausting recursor resources.

item.title: CVE-2026-123607 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.25.0-alpha.3 through 0.25.2 and hickory-net before 0.26.1 contain an unbounded loop vulnerability in DnssecDnsHandle NSEC3 closest-encloser proof validation when the SOA owner is not an ancestor of the QNAME. Upstream attackers can return NoData or NXDomain responses with a cross-zone SOA record to panic debug builds or exhaust memory in release builds.

item.title: CVE-2026-123608 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | Hickory DNS hickory-proto from 0.3.1 before 0.26.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in BinEncoder that allows remote attackers to exhaust CPU through quadratic-time name compression. Attackers can send malicious DNS messages with many records that add many candidate labels and trigger repeated linear scans during encoding, amplifying CPU exhaustion.

item.title: CVE-2026-123609 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 4.1
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 4.1 | Rustls before 0.23.46 and 0.24.0-dev.1 before 0.24.0-dev.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability where derived Debug formatting of client session values exposes secret key material. Custom ClientSessionStore implementations that log Tls12ClientSessionValue or Tls13ClientSessionValue can leak TLS 1.2 master secrets or TLS 1.3 resumption PSKs to log readers.

item.title: CVE-2026-123610 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | rustls before 0.23.46 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation flaw in its optional Brotli certificate decompression, which limits decompressed output size but accepts an input-selected large history window. Malicious peers can send a certificate with a five-byte Brotli header requesting up to 1 GiB before authentication, aborting Brotli-enabled clients or client-authenticating servers whose allocator cannot satisfy the request.

item.title: CVE-2026-123611 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | rustls before 0.23.46 contains a key exchange downgrade vulnerability that allows network attackers to poison the per-server-name key-exchange group record via an unauthenticated ServerHello. Attackers can answer one connection with a ServerHello selecting X25519, causing later ClientHellos to send only classical shares and lose post-quantum confidentiality.

item.title: CVE-2026-123612 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 4.6
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 4.6 | rustls 0.23.44 and 0.23.45 contain an information disclosure vulnerability that sends application data buffered before the handshake completes to the client-facing server when Encrypted Client Hello is rejected. Because start_traffic() queues plaintext from ClientConnection::writer() before sending the ech_required alert, the authenticated public_name server receives data intended for the inner server.

item.title: CVE-2026-123613 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | Rustls from 0.23.13 before 0.23.45 accepts TLS 1.3 handshake messages at the wrong encryption level when they follow a key-changing message in the same record, because Deframer::aligned does not enforce RFC 8446 record-boundary alignment. A peer or on-path attacker can pack a plaintext EncryptedExtensions with the ServerHello, which rustls accepts unencrypted.

item.title: CVE-2026-123614 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 9.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 9.3 | imgproxy from 4.0.0 before 4.0.16 contains an integer overflow in the ICO loader that allows remote attackers to trigger a heap buffer overflow via a crafted data_size value. Attackers can submit a crafted ICO image whose data_size wraps the allocation in vips/icoload.c, corrupting heap memory to crash the process or achieve code execution.

item.title: CVE-2026-123615 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | imgproxy 3.3.0 before 4.0.17 contains an out-of-bounds heap read and write in the ICO loader's BMP header reconstruction (vips_foreign_load_ico_header in vips/icoload.c) when an ICO entry declares a tiny data size, causing unvalidated header fields to be read and written past the allocated buffer. Unauthenticated remote attackers can supply a crafted ICO image to corrupt adjacent heap chunk metadata, triggering a glibc abort that crashes the worker.

item.title: CVE-2026-123616 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | imgproxy from 3.3.0 before 4.0.16 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability in the ICO loader that fails to validate the data_size field. Attackers can supply a crafted 23-byte ICO file declaring a ~4GB data_size to trigger memory exhaustion and worker crashes without authentication.

item.title: CVE-2026-124422 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3 | SunEditor from 3.0.0 before 3.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in html.clean() that rebuilds iframes from data-se-iframe-holder-attrs JSON without filtering srcdoc or uppercase SRC keys. Attackers can inject crafted HTML through paste, html.set, or html.insert to execute script in the host page origin when victims load or paste the content.

item.title: CVE-2026-114713 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.6
item.description: Sunday 8 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.6 | The labeled-response module in UnrealIRCd 6.0.0 before 6.2.7.1 does not escape the IRCv3 "label" message tag when echoing it into replies, which allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority.
